keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row for the burgraviate). The page gives no area and no town list ('Cadolzburg: not on page'); it says the burgraviate 'was partitioned to form Brandenburg-Ansbach and Brandenburg-Bayreuth'. The stand-in is the union of the circles principality-of-ansbach (28 km at Ansbach) and principality-of-bayreuth (32 km at Bayreuth and 20 km at Kulmbach) use, soft; the Imperial castle at Nuremberg itself (the office sold to the city in 1427/1440) is not drawn.

ledger.note: 1105: the burgraves. Infobox 'Burgraviate granted to House of Raabs: 1105' ('First documentary mention: 1050'); the article says the burgraviate existed 'from the early 12th to the late 15th centuries'. The page gives no land for 1105.
1192: the Hohenzollern. Frederick I 'took office in 1192' (listed '1192-1200/1204'), becoming burgrave through his union with Sophia, daughter of Conrad II of Raabs.
1363: princely status. Infobox 'Raised to princely status: 1363'.

21 January 1398: Bayreuth. 'The principality arose upon the death of the Hohenzollern burgrave Frederick V of Nuremberg on 21 January 1398' (infobox 'Partitioned from Burgraviate of Nuremberg: 21 January 1398'); John III received Bayreuth.

21 January 1398: Ansbach. 'The principality was established following the death of Frederick V, Burgrave of Nuremberg, on 21 January 1398'; his lands were split between his sons Frederick VI (Ansbach) and John III (Bayreuth). The Burgraviate page dates the partition to 1440 in its infobox and the sale of the office to the city to 1427/1440.

certainty.note: The page gives no area, no towns and no boundary; the lands of the later principalities stand in for the burgraviate.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (3 pages: its own plus the Ansbach and Bayreuth pages already opened for those dossiers; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no row for the burgraviate.

SCOPE. 1105 (infobox, House of Raabs) to 21 January 1398 (death of Frederick V, from the Ansbach and Bayreuth pages, whose dossiers found their principalities that day). The Burgraviate page itself dates the partition to 1440 and the sale of the burgraviate to the city (except the Blutgericht) to 1427/1440 (infobox '1427 1440'); the page also says Frederick VI was 'Margrave of Brandenburg-Kulmbach from 1420', 'Elector of Brandenburg from 1415, Margrave of Brandenburg from 1417', so the later steps are the Hohenzollern margraviates. The 1398 end follows the two principality pages; the 1440 date is flagged here.

SHAPES. The union of the Ansbach and Bayreuth circles. The page gives no town but Nuremberg. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Nuremberg' (circle not drawn), 'Cadolzburg' (not on the page).

NOT SETTLED. (1) 1398 against 1440 for the partition; (2) the burgraviate's land in 1105 and 1192; (3) 1427 against 1440 for the sale of the office; (4) no area; (5) the Second Margrave War, the 1388 Städtekrieg and the 1449 conflict are not on the page.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new.
